## ISO 9001:2015 — 8.1 Operational planning and control

**Standard / control:** ISO 9001:2015, 8.1 Operational planning and control
**Repository:** `xianix-team/the-agent` (local clone)
**Baseline:** `main` @ `1d45f72` (clean working tree)
**Sources file:** `implicit git-repo` (no `.xianix/operation-sources.yaml`, `compliance/operation-sources.yaml` or `--sources` found)
**Git scope:** `full repository`
**Products / services in scope:** Xianix Agent control plane (`99xio/xianix-agent` image); Xianix Executor (`99xio/xianix-executor` image); AI-DLC lifecycle service (label-triggered agents on customer repositories); Rules Optimizer chat
**Processes in scope:** Service design (architecture and design docs); Development and merge; Executor build, test and publish; Agent build and publish; Deployment to the Azure VM; Tenant secret management; Operations and monitoring; AI-DLC lifecycle (service delivery); Incident handling and rollback
**Report date:** `2026-09-21`
**Overall 8.1 status:** `Partial`

---

### Sources used

| Id | Provider | Roles | Verdict | Artifacts | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| codebase | git-repo | all (implicit fallback) | ok | 27 | The published documentation site (a separate repository) and any issue tracker are not declared, so they were not fetched. |

---

### Summary

The Xianix Agent delivers a multi-tenant control plane that turns platform webhooks into isolated Claude Code executions, plus an executor image and an AI-DLC lifecycle service built on label-driven agents. Planning is documented in depth: architecture objectives, a tenant-isolation design, a rules specification, a webhook guide, an AI-DLC process with explicit human review gates, and Azure infrastructure and deployment runbooks. Controls are strong for the executor: shellcheck and a hermetic integration-test tier gate every tagged publish. They're weak for the agent image, which publishes on tag without running its 150 unit tests. Most commits reach `main` without a pull request, releases have no notes, and deployment always pulls `:latest`. Some maintained documents no longer match the code. There's no incident or rollback procedure. No core obligation is a Gap, so the overall 8.1 status is Partial.

---

There's no versioned requirement set, and no customer or statutory requirements (e.g. data handling for tenant repositories). |

Internal development, review and release criteria aren't written down. |

### Change control

**Planned changes**

Significant changes are planned in design documents (`Docs/tenant-isolation-design.md` starts from a problem statement and goals; `Docs/ai-dlc-ping-pong.md` states it supersedes the earlier triggers). Releases are semver-tagged, and executor releases pass automated gates. There is no decision-record index, no change log, and most changes are committed directly to `main` (4 merge commits among 36 commits since 2026-08-01). Tag names are inconsistent (`vv1.8.0` onwards).

**Unintended changes**

`not found` as a process. Operations guidance covers viewing logs and restarting the service (`Docs/azure-deployment.md`). `Scripts/deploy.sh` always pulls `:latest`, so returning to a known-good version needs manual steps that aren't documented. There's no incident intake, post-incident review or corrective-action record.
